baseline_first_test.proof: B_(+2) for a post-V branch depends on the same tag's opposite branch or an empty support class on the frozen positive q-domain; I1/I2 cannot alter another tag's fixed probe.

cartesian_multiplicity_warning: Global product-weighted history marginals can all rescale when one tag loses a branch. This independent multiplicative factor is retained diagnostically but is not a causal dependency edge and is excluded from RESP_TAG.

finite_information_theorem.consequence: for fixed D,T,q this bound is independent of N; fixed finite local signature + fixed return rounds cannot establish system-spanning response as N grows
finite_information_theorem.statement: Let P be a fixed finite H-probe set with D=max|r|, and let T be a fixed number of scheduler rounds. If every current tag state differs from its aligned base by at most T H-actions, a one-tag intervention can create a dependency edge i<-j only when |q(j-i)|<=D+2T. After T rounds, participant tags lie in a T-fold composition of this finite dependency set.
finite_information_theorem.typing: relational dependency-word bound only; not a metric ball

full_source_local_cloud: Even reading the complete finite macrostep lineage of the same tag creates no cross-tag dependency by itself; under I2 its participant count remains 1 unless an additional cross-tag/global aggregate is introduced.
